settingText: PRESENT — approach to the Core-Forge, the place Adrian says the Reset was enacted. Modern construction occupies ancient foundations that are increasingly visible through one another.
summary: Theo, Rae and Adrian reach the site where the forgotten war was erased from lived continuity. Present architecture no longer fully hides the ancient place beneath it. Adrian intends to repeat the Reset if the public memory crisis continues widening.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Theo, Rae and Adrian approach the Core-Forge through modern construction laid over ancient foundations. They have come because Neo-Vectra's memory crisis is spreading faster than local measures can contain it.
Panel 2 — Theo steps ahead and blocks Adrian's path: 'You brought us here to do it again.' Adrian stops at the threshold with both hands visible.
Panel 3 — Adrian says, 'I brought you here because I don't know what else stops this.' He does not move toward the central scar.
Panel 4 — Rae answers, 'Neither did I yesterday.' Adrian says, 'You stopped.' Rae: 'Eventually.' Their exchange is grounded in Rae's recent policy failure, not moral superiority.
Panel 5 — Wide threshold panel. All three face the same scarred chamber entrance while keeping visible distance from one another; no one touches a device or explains a mechanism.

dialogueInline.text: You brought us here to do it again.
I brought you here because I don't know what else stops this.

summary: Kyn debuts as one exhausted person describing the war through specific ordinary suffering rather than strategic abstraction.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Final ancient council in a plain neutral chamber. Everyone looks exhausted by years of knowing one another through war. Kyn enters without ceremony and takes an ordinary seat.
Panel 2 — Mero: 'Tell me what I'm missing.' Kyn: 'Sleep.' Let the answer land as bodily truth before philosophy.
Panel 3 — Mero presses. Kyn refuses the abstraction and begins with children waking afraid of battles they cannot see.

summary: Kyn, Oryon and Arbiter argue over suffering, prevention and responsibility before the full ancient council assembles.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Kyn describes children waking in fear while the page shows one ordinary family awake in a quiet room with no battle visible.
Panel 2 — Kyn describes a stranger seeing an old faction mark and recoiling from someone they do not know; another survivor carries a dead companion through a doorway.
Panel 3 — Kyn says, 'That's what the war feels like now.' Keep every example grounded in faces, touch and ordinary spaces.
Panel 4 — Oryon answers, 'Then we stop it before it reaches another city.' His fear is personal, not abstract calculation.
Panel 5 — Arbiter says, 'We've been saying that for years.' Hold the exhausted council in a wide still composition.

dialogueInline.text: Children wake up screaming in rooms where nothing is happening.
Someone sees a mark on a stranger and remembers the same mark on the person who hurt them three worlds ago.
That's what the war feels like now.
Then we stop it before it reaches another city.
We've been saying that for years.

summary: Theo and Rae begin experiencing their ancient selves continuously rather than as discrete visions. They do not converse across time; each present action restores the remembered context of an ancient action.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Present Theo walks the Core-Forge corridor. Match his stride and camera position to ancient Theo on the next panel.
Panel 2 — Ancient Theo carries papers through the same geometry. No ghost overlay; the match represents one person's restored continuity.
Panel 3 — Present Theo says, 'I know this hallway.' Rae answers, 'So do I.' Their recognition is bodily and immediate.
Panel 4 — Match ancient Rae waiting outside the familiar door with present Rae occupying the same position in modern construction.
Panel 5 — Theo says, 'I hated that door.' His present body leans away from the same threshold his ancient self used to cross.
Panel 6 — Rae says, 'I used to wait outside it.' Hold her in the same waiting position across both timelines.

dialogueInline.text: I used to wait outside it.

summary: The surviving ancient principals gather with Flux's place empty, each old virtue now visibly carrying its failure mode.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Wide final-council composition with the established participants present as people who know one another.
Panel 2 — Flux's familiar place remains empty; do not add an unidentified mystery figure.
Panel 3 — Afterlight says, 'I can't repair all of this.' Atlas answers, 'Then we stop doing it.'
Panel 4 — Starbreaker asks, 'And wait for the next one to hit?' His fear comes from accumulated failures rather than doctrine.
Panel 5 — Redlin answers, 'We've caused enough of them ourselves.' Let the old relationship history sharpen both lines.

summary: The argument tightens until Kyn points out that they are still waiting for a clean option that does not exist.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Oryon says, 'Waiting changes the outcome too.' He is afraid of futures he has seen, not delivering doctrine.
Panel 2 — Arbiter places both hands on the table and says, 'Whatever this room does, someone owns it.'
Panel 3 — Around Arbiter, the others avoid eye contact; Flux's empty place remains visible and no seat offers a moral center.
Panel 4 — Kyn says, 'There isn't a clean one. Stop waiting for it.' End on the full exhausted group in silence.

summary: Adrian offers to close the scar again while Theo insists stolen memory must be restored rather than erased.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Central scar chamber. Ancient and modern material overlap, but there is no obvious device waiting to be operated.
Panel 2 — Adrian stands on the worn floor mark where he once made the irreversible choice.
Panel 3 — Adrian says, 'I can close it.' Theo steps between him and the scar.
Panel 4 — Theo says, 'You mean erase it.' Rae remains off to one side, watching both men claim the center of the room.
Panel 5 — Adrian says, 'I mean stop this before people start killing for memories they received yesterday.' Theo answers, 'They were stolen from them.'

dialogueInline.text: I mean stop this before people start killing for memories they received yesterday.

summary: Rae recognizes that forced forgetting and forced restoration both assume the right to decide what other people should carry.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Rae steps toward Theo as he prepares to force the scar open and says, 'You can't force it open.'
Panel 2 — Theo asks, 'Why not?' while keeping one hand near the physical scar.
Panel 3 — Rae says, 'Because I just watched what happens when we decide people can't handle their own memories.' Her recent Neo-Vectra mistake is the immediate evidence.
Panel 4 — Theo answers, 'I'm doing the opposite.' Adrian remains on the far side of the chamber, making the visual symmetry obvious.
Panel 5 — Rae says, 'I don't think you are,' and moves fully between Theo and Adrian.
Panel 6 — End with Rae centered, Theo on one side and Adrian on the other, while the scar chamber recedes behind them.

dialogueInline.text: Because I just watched what happens when we decide people can't handle their own memories.

settingText: PAST — outside the final council, Kyn and Afterlight share a quiet moment while the others continue arguing behind the door.
summary: Kyn asks Afterlight whether people can recover if the war ends. Afterlight says recovery is possible only if they stop demanding that recovery restore what was lost. Their exchange gives the Reset debate a human alternative to victory.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Outside the council door, Kyn and Afterlight sit somewhere unceremonious while muffled argument continues behind them. Kyn asks, 'If it stopped tonight, could they heal?' Afterlight answers, 'Some.'
Panel 2 — Kyn asks, 'That's all?' Afterlight answers, 'Some is the honest answer.' They remain beside the same exhausted survivor rather than turning toward each other theatrically.
Panel 3 — Kyn says, 'I keep wanting more than that.' Afterlight looks at her own tired hands and the unfinished repairs around them.
Panel 4 — Afterlight says, 'So do I. I keep promising more than I can repair.' End on the two of them sharing the same exhausted quiet despite faction differences.

dialogueInline.text: If it stopped tonight, could they heal?
I keep wanting more than that.
So do I. I keep promising more than I can repair.

summary: Ancient Arbiter asks Rae whether she will record the Reset decision; Rae agrees but refuses to rename coercion as mercy.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Present Rae reaches a familiar threshold in the convergence corridor.
Panel 2 — Match her posture to ancient Rae seated beside Arbiter during the final council.
Panel 3 — Ancient Arbiter asks, 'If Mero authorizes it, will you record the decision?'
Panel 4 — Rae answers, 'Yes.' Her participation is ordinary and professional, which makes it harder to disown.
Panel 5 — Arbiter says, 'You disagree.' Rae answers, 'I disagree with calling it mercy.'
Panel 6 — Hold ancient Rae and Arbiter close over the same marked ruling sheet, both hands sharing the edge of the table rather than facing off.

summary: Rae records the decision in exact language without pretending she has found a clean alternative to it.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Arbiter asks, 'What should I call it?' Ancient Rae looks down at the ruling before answering.
Panel 2 — Rae says, 'What it is. We're taking something from everyone because we couldn't stop.'
Panel 3 — Arbiter asks, 'And if it ends the war?' The question lands without changing the physical work in front of them.
Panel 4 — Rae answers, 'Then write that too,' and returns the ruling sheet to Arbiter.
Panel 5 — Match present Rae gripping the same table edge, carrying the remembered compromise without pretending it was clean.
Panel 6 — End on present Rae understanding that ancient moral clarity did not spare her from participation.

dialogueInline.text: What it is. We're taking something from everyone because we couldn't stop.

summary: Mero asks ancient Adrian to execute the Reset because Adrian crossed every factional boundary and understands what is being taken.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — After the council, Mero and ancient Adrian remain alone in a plain room with two chairs, a table and an open doorway.
Panel 2 — No machine, schematic, controls or glowing apparatus is visible anywhere in the room.
Panel 3 — Mero: 'I need you to do it.' Adrian: 'No.' The refusal is immediate and personal.
Panel 4 — Mero: 'You know every road between them.' Adrian: 'I carried messages. I opened doors.' Show the burden of being the person who moved between all sides.

summary: Adrian invokes neutrality and Mero destroys that refuge: carrying every side's messages did not place Adrian outside responsibility.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Mero says, 'You watched us use every door you opened to find another battlefield.' He gestures toward the open council-room door and then back toward Adrian.
Panel 2 — Adrian remains still across from him, physically between two open corridors that once led to different factions.
Panel 3 — Adrian says, 'That doesn't make this mine.' Mero steps closer but does not treat him like a technician receiving an order.
Panel 4 — Mero answers, 'No. It belongs to all of us.' Adrian finally looks directly at him.
Panel 5 — Mero continues, 'I'm asking you because you crossed every line between us and kept going.' End on Adrian alone between the two open corridors.

dialogueInline.text: You watched us use every door you opened to find another battlefield.
No. It belongs to all of us. I'm asking you because you crossed every line between us and kept going.

summary: Theo recovers his final ancient contribution. Mero asked whether people could become something other than the war if the memory of it were removed. Theo answered that they might, but warned that taking the choice from them would become another act of the war. Mero proceeded anyway.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Present Theo stands outside the same door where ancient Theo once waited; past and present occupy matching compositions without labels.
Panel 2 — Ancient Mero sits heavily on the bench and asks, 'If they forgot us, could they become something else?'
Panel 3 — Junior Theo stands beside him with papers under one arm and answers, 'Maybe,' without certainty.
Panel 4 — Mero says, 'That's more hope than I've heard all year.' Theo answers, 'It's not permission.'
Panel 5 — Mero says, 'I know.' Theo asks, 'Do you?' The familiarity between them makes the question sharper than a speech.
Panel 6 — Return to present Theo remembering that he saw possible freedom in forgetting and still warned that imposed forgetting would repeat the war's coercion.

summary: Rae physically interrupts Theo and Adrian, breaking the repeated composition and refusing both forced restoration and forced forgetting.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Match ancient Adrian continuing the Reset with present Adrian preparing to repeat his own old choice.
Panel 2 — Rae releases Theo and turns toward Adrian before he can complete the present gesture.
Panel 3 — Adrian says, 'Rae—' She cuts him off: 'You too.' The present composition visibly diverges from the ancient one.
Panel 4 — Rae says, 'Nobody chooses for everyone again.' Both men stop.
Panel 5 — End on the broken matched composition: no one completes either universal intervention, and the scar remains physically unresolved.

settingText: PRESENT — intercut ordinary locations after the Core-Forge choice: Olyria-Prime worksite, Zenith archives, Tyrellis transit platform, Neo-Vectra civic route, then the Core-Forge exit.
summary: Nothing resolves cleanly, but the consequence is shown through people already known: Vark protects workers rather than reporting impossible recollections, Calum leaves returning records visible, the Tyrellis worker's partner stays with him, and the Neo-Vectra couple crosses the reopened route together. The trio accepts that memory and conflict must now be handled socially rather than universally controlled.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Olyria-Prime shift room. Vark listens while one worker insists they remember a corridor that does not exist and another remembers nothing. Vark quietly closes an incident form before anyone can turn the contradiction into a disciplinary report, then pushes the coffee pot toward them. Ordinary shift noise continues.

Panel 2 — Zenith archives. Calum stands beside a junior archivist as another erased record repopulates. Instead of removing it, he moves his hand away from the delete control and leaves the entry visible. Around them clerks keep working, visibly uncertain about the new policy.

Panel 3 — Tyrellis transit platform. The same TRANSIT WORKER from Issue 6 sits with the same PARTNER; the worker is still grieving the impossible brother while the partner covers both work radios and stays beside him. Trains keep arriving.

Panel 4 — Neo-Vectra. The recurring MAN and WOMAN from Issue 7 walk through the reopened route together carrying the same bags and keys. Behind them, officials replace recovered-affiliation barriers with ordinary behavior-based security and open access.

Panel 5 — Back at the Core-Forge exit. Theo looks at the unchanged scar chamber behind them: 'So what happens now?' Rae is already walking toward the voices outside: 'People remember what they remember.'

Panel 6 — Adrian: 'And if it starts the war again?' Rae: 'Then we stop the war.' Adrian: 'That's not the same thing.' Rae: 'Exactly.' End on the trio joining the occupied corridor rather than standing alone in the chamber.

dialogueInline.text: And if it starts the war again?

directionInline.text: PAGE ARCHITECTURE — G6; exactly 6 panels. Six stable rectilinear panels, one clear location per panel, no fractured-memory borders. This is a social-resolution page, not an abstract montage: every location must contain ongoing work, relationships and ordinary civic behavior.

RECURRING-PRESENT PAYOFF — Panel 1 Vark is the same Olyria foreman from Issue 1; Panel 2 Calum is the same Zenith magistrate; Panel 3 is the same Tyrellis transit worker and partner from Issue 6; Panel 4 is the same Neo-Vectra couple from Issue 7. Preserve identifying clothing/props where possible so the reader reads continuity immediately.

summary: The trio sees that a familiar region of the night sky is simply wrong: stars everyone remembers are absent. Nobody can tell whether they were erased, belonged only to replacement history, or were lost when continuity returned. Reality's memory has consequences beyond personal recollection.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Quiet observation window after the immediate crisis. Theo, Rae and Adrian look at a familiar region of deep space. No alarms or instruments announce the problem. Theo points through the observation window: 'Were those always gone?' A familiar star cluster has a clean dark gap where several stars should be; render it as ordinary black sky with missing points of light and no glow or distortion.

Panel 2 — Rae: 'No.' She steps close to the glass and fixes on the dark gap, face still and certain; Adrian watches Rae instead of the sky. Adrian: 'I don't know.' Give the admission room; for once he does not hide uncertainty behind protection or authority. Theo: 'You finally said it.' Adrian: 'Get used to hearing it.'

Panel 3 — Final wide panel: three small people facing a sky with a meaningful absence. Truth has returned unevenly; certainty has diminished. Do not reveal Flux, Regent or a technical explanation for the missing stars.
